target_customer: Donors and members funding civil liberties work; beneficiaries are people whose rights are at stake
problem: A flood of online donations in early 2017 left the ACLU needing technology and fundraising capacity to scale its response.
business_model: Nonprofit funded by member dues, contributions and private foundation grants

founders.name: Anthony Romero
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; the ACLU itself dates to 1920 so he is its executive director, not its founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: Not a technology product. The YC engagement supplied pro bono engineering to modernize operations.

defensibility.rationale: A century of litigation history, a national brand and membership of over 500000 are hard to replicate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No one tried to absorb the ACLU's role; it remains independent.

market_need_then: In late January 2017 the ACLU raised about 24 million dollars online from over 350000 donations after challenging the travel ban, per coverage, creating a need to scale.

branding.name_origin: Initials of American Civil Liberties Union

identity.logo: Wordmark drawn by Tobias Frere-Jones of studio Open from an archival 1984 to 2001 wordmark, replacing a 2002 Statue of Liberty inspired identity
identity.visual_style: Bold red and blue with the Century typeface used for Supreme Court briefs
identity.voice_and_tone: Urgent, principled; 'Defend the rights of all people nationwide'

branding.brand_signature: The red and blue wordmark and campaign graphics

rebrands.from: 2002 identity by Sylvia Harris and team
rebrands.why: First update since 2002 per Fast Company; exact year not confirmed

branding.community_and_virality: Press on the brand identity in Fast Company and Print; donor surge of 2017 was widely covered.

brand_strength.rationale: A century old household name that drew tens of millions of dollars in days in 2017 and has dedicated design guidelines and press about its identity.

outcome_analysis: The ACLU joined YC Winter 2017 as a nonprofit after a donation surge following its travel ban litigation, receiving funding, mentors and engineering help to scale. It is not a startup, so venture style outcomes do not apply; it remains active with over 500 staff and a century of brand equity. Success is driven by the brand and an existing donor base.
notes: Not a startup: nonprofit founded 1920, included in YC's nonprofit track. The YC support amount conflicts: ABA Journal says 200000 dollars; Axios says 100000 was YC's standard nonprofit donation and the rest came from Sam Altman personally. Recorded as a grant at 200000. The Open redesign year is not confirmed so the rebrand date 2017 is approximate. The 24 million figure is from news summaries seen in search. Competitors are not applicable, so the list is empty. Founded year left null because the schema rejects 1920; the ACLU was founded in 1920.
